name: Waypoint Lamps
tagline: The flight console with its lamps where the family's hands go: every stop on the flight plan carries its day, every tick is a pilot lamp, and every instrument has its placard.
concept: Flight Console with its lamps where the family's hands go. Waypoint Lamps keeps Master Caution's console (slate bays, the readout rail, the master caution, the flight plan, the jewelled lamps, the meter, the radar, the roll of light, the lit bus) and grafts three features that each replace a code the family had to learn: the day of the month as a large light numeral leading every Coming up row and carried on its waypoint ring on the route (Grid Console, Attract Mode); every tick and checkbox a pilot lamp in a 44px key, amber in its well when late, the jewel when done (Headland Light), so the crew board's lamps go; and an engraved placard with a breathing lamp under each instrument (Night Gallery), which takes the explanations off the glass. The route is grease pencil on a plotting board, a warm bone in place of violet. Every ring on the route has its row, the next plan first and lit, and every day on every page is the same light numeral.
companions: Slate (#111716) for every bay under one 2px top rule; route bone (#cdc1a0, flown #6b665a, drawn as a dotted trail) only for the route's lines and waypoint rings, the month word beside a day numeral, and the dashed leg onto the next sheet: grounded, low-chroma, one job (time still ahead); steel (#6f8596, cap #a9c4d8) for 'here' (a 2px cap and the jewel, no fill) and the pilot lamps' open rim; pewter for off and flown; amber (#e3a651) only for the caution lamp and edge, and late (the bar in a tick's well, a row's edge, the words); clay for the restaurant swatch, mulberry for the seasonal.
